content.text: I have investigated all responsive locations. No restrictive covenant binds IBM anywhere in the Agreement.

input.quote: 1) providing to others products or services which may be competitive with products or services of the Discloser; 2) providing products or services to others who compete with the Discloser; or 3) assigning its employees in any way it may choose.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on IBM, so it sits at our preferred position. Searches for compete/competing, exclusivity, field-of-use, territory, sole-source and requirements language returned no covenant binding IBM. The only competition-related provisions run the other way or are neutral: (i) the confidentiality terms at p1490-p1491 expressly preserve each recipient's freedom to provide competitive products or services and to assign employees as it chooses; (ii) Section 5.1(b)(v) (p0116) is a mutual change-of-control termination trigger, not a restraint on the businesses IBM may operate; and (iii) Section 14.18 "Restrictions and Limitations" (p0995) restricts MSL's use of IBM property, which benefits us. The Attachment 1 Section 7.4 mechanics (p0767-p0775) are disclosure/right-to-match provisions that expressly permit IBM to move Product to the third party if MSL cannot match; that is MFN territory, not exclusivity, and is not flagged here. No redline required.
